name: Elevance Health
description: Elevance Health is one of the largest US health insurers, serving about 45.2 million medical members at 2025-12-31 through Blue Cross and Blue Shield licensed plans in 14 states (including California, Colorado, Connecticut, Georgia, Indiana, Kentucky) plus Wellpoint-branded Medicaid, Medicare and commercial plans elsewhere. Employers, individuals and governments (Medicaid and Medicare Advantage via CMS) pay premiums and Elevance pays the medical claims, keeping the difference. It also runs two fast-growing services arms: CarelonRx, a pharmacy benefit manager that fills prescriptions for its own plans and outside clients (core services delegated to CVS's Caremark), and Carelon Services, which delivers care and clinical services. Much of CarelonRx and Carelon Services revenue comes from Elevance's own health plans and is eliminated on consolidation ($41.7 billion in 2025), so segment revenues add up to far more than the $197.6 billion reported.

businessLines.name: Health Benefits
businessLines.how: Customers pay monthly premiums (or administrative fees for self-funded employers) and Elevance pays members' medical claims; the margin is the gap between premium and claims plus overhead. Profit swings with medical cost trend versus premium rates, and government rates (Medicare Advantage, Medicaid) are set by CMS and states.

businessLines.name: CarelonRx
businessLines.how: Charges health plans and employers per prescription filled and a spread between what it pays pharmacies and drug makers and what it bills clients, plus rebate retention and mail/specialty dispensing margin. Volume (scripts) and drug price drive revenue; a large part comes from Elevance's own members.
businessLines.description: Pharmacy benefit management: mail-order and specialty pharmacy, formulary and claims services for Elevance's own plans and external health-plan clients. Core services are delegated to CaremarkPCS Health (CVS) under an agreement.
